about: What the Kotlin backend's Lua answers for what `sce-build`'s frontend
EMITTED, case by case, against the shared table beside this file.
This is the OTHER route into a Lua engine, and it is not the one
`kotlin_lua_divergences.json` measures. That file is about the engine's
input adapter rewriting the author's ECMAScript on the spot; this one is
about the Lua the frontend already produced, read from
`ecma262_emitted_lua.json`. Go, Python and the Rust frontend suite have
asked their own Lua that question since the emission existed and each
found defects their W3C suite could not see. Nothing on this backend
asked it until `LoweredEcma262Test` did, which is why
`docs/SCE_LUA_TRANSLATION_SEAM.md` recorded that "the frontend answers
all 98 cases" was a statement about `sce-build` plus somebody else's Lua.
TWO ARRAYS, because two different things are wrong and collapsing them
would hide the smaller one behind the larger.
`unreachable` — the case never reaches the engine as the frontend wrote
it. This backend has NO lowered entry point: every method on
`LuaScriptEngine` runs `EcmaScriptToLuaTransformer` over its argument
first, because the generated Kotlin hands the engine the author's text at
every site (`sce-codegen --script-engine lua -l kotlin` refuses, naming
the sites still to move). For most cases the rewriter happens to leave
the frontend's Lua alone and the measurement is honest. For these it does
not, and the changes are destructive rather than cosmetic — a Lua table
key `{["k"] = 1}` comes out `{{"k"} = 1}`, a one-based `a[1]` is shifted
again to `a[2]`, `table.concat(xs, ",")` becomes `_concat(table, xs,
",")`. Whatever the engine answers for one of these is an answer about
the rewriter's handling of Lua text. Counting it as a lowering result
would be measuring the thing this route exists to remove.
`divergences` — the case DOES reach the engine unchanged, and the answer
is still not what ECMA-262 says. These are the real findings, and the
array is EMPTY today.
⚠ It held two, and the reason they left is worth more than the two.
This file said they were a defect of the LOWERED route — the emitted
setup assigns without `var` (`Var1 = 1`, `total = 0`), so a guard that
learns names from the rewriter's handling of `var` never learns them.
That reading was wrong about where the defect lived. The guard
(`LuaScriptEngine.isUndeclaredSimpleVariable`) asked only whether the
SESSION had declared a name, while its C++ sibling
(`SCE::isUndeclaredIdentifier`) also asks the Lua interpreter whether the
name is a live global. `executeScript` files nothing in `declaredVars` on
either route, so the same two cases were declared divergences in
`kotlin_lua_divergences.json` as well — the ROUTE was never what they had
in common. Giving the Kotlin guard the global lookup its C++ sibling
already had closed them in both files at once.
The lesson to keep: a defect that shows up on one route is not thereby a
defect OF that route. Both lists named these two, and nothing compared
the two lists until something had to.
BOTH ARRAYS EMPTY IS THE TERMINAL STATE, and there is a path to it: the
lowered seam. `IScriptEngine` carries it on the C++ side already — an
expression arrives as a (lowered, source) pair and a Lua engine takes the
lowered arm — and the day `ScxmlScriptEngine` carries the same thing,
`unreachable` empties because the rewriter leaves the path, and
`divergences` empties with it because a lowered entry point trusts the
frontend's scope analysis instead of re-deriving it from `var`. Neither
array can be emptied by editing this file: `LoweredEcma262Test` holds
each in BOTH directions, so an entry that stops describing the backend
fails as loudly as one that starts.
`source` and `clause` together identify a case: the shared table asks
`a && b` under two clauses, and a list keyed on the expression alone
would let one entry cover a case nobody looked at.
NOT a `diverges_on` list, and deliberately a separate file from the two
beside it. Those enumerate what an engine answers differently and their
`paths` key is derived from what the code generator can emit; this one
also enumerates what the suite could not ASK, which is a different claim
with a different repair. Merging them would give one array two meanings
and no reader could tell which an entry carried.
